speaker: Mr Saktiandi Supaat (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
text: I have one follow-up question with regard to my last question about mitigating policies in the scenario where, if COE prices actually do rise over the next few years or following the policy introduction, will the Ministry of Transport (MOT) look into considering potentially introducing COE subsidies or rebates, for example, for families or citizens with disability in the future, for example, alleviating some of cost increases as a result of the COE increase?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Indeed, it is a pertinent question that is in the minds of many.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: While our current vehicle quota system is not a perfect solution, it is still the most appropriate at this point in time to allocate a limited and non-basic resource, such as vehicle ownership.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: The Government is very mindful of the aspiration and wishes of Singaporeans to enjoy a high degree of mobility.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Like what I have said in my reply, we will continue to invest heavily to improve our public transport system – more rail lines and bus routes – and also trying innovative models of transportation, such as private hire car services.

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: Hopefully, this will help reduce the need to own a car.

speaker: Dr Lim Wee Kiak (Sembawang)
text: Will MOT consider leveraging an extra certain percentage if you buy a second COE under your own name?

speaker: Dr Lam Pin Min
text: With regard to the question on how many families own more than one car, I do not have the figures with me right now at this point in time but I think this question has been answered in a past Parliamentary Question and I would be able to provide the answer subsequently to the Member.
